questions.prompt: Which prayer asks for daily bread?
questions.explanation: These words come from the Our Father, which also asks for forgiveness and deliverance from evil.
questions.clue: Give us this day our daily bread;

questions.prompt: At both sides of the lower waist, the index and middle fingers tap against each thumb twice. Which sign fits?
questions.explanation: Diaper uses matching modified-3 handshapes at the lower waist. The paired taps resemble fastening the tabs.

questions.prompt: Your baby loses interest halfway through a short Bible story. What next?
questions.clue: He was enjoying your voice but now turns away and wants a change.
options: Keep reading the remaining pages so the prayer routine has a clear finish.
Switch immediately to a more animated story to regain his attention.
Finish the small moment and try another story during a calmer awake time.
questions.explanation: An infant’s Bible moment can be short and responsive. You are making Scripture familiar; there is no lesson he must finish.

questions.prompt: Which sign is shown in this clip?
questions.clue: Watch the hand open and close.
questions.explanation: This is Milk: the curved hand closes into a fist and relaxes again. The movement comes from the hand, with the forearm staying quiet.

questions.prompt: What makes a bedtime blessing easier to keep?
questions.clue: You want prayer to remain part of family life during busy early weeks.
options: Reserve the blessing for evenings when both parents finish care together.
Choose a different prayer each night so the routine stays interesting.
Use a short blessing that either parent can offer during bedtime care.
questions.explanation: A small, familiar blessing fits ordinary care. Parents can offer it together or take turns.

questions.prompt: In Ave Maria's Our Father, which word comes next?
questions.explanation: The line asks for God's will to be done on earth as it is in heaven.
questions.clue: Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done on earth as it is in

questions.prompt: Beyond the Baptism day, what is a godparent’s continuing role?
options: Help the child grow in the Catholic faith through lasting support.
Take primary responsibility for teaching faith in place of the parents.
Organize the child’s Baptism anniversary celebrations each year.
questions.explanation: Think about prayer, presence, and support over time when choosing godparents. Confirm sponsor eligibility with your parish.

questions.prompt: Which mystery recalls Gabriel announcing that Mary would become the Mother of God?
questions.explanation: The Annunciation is the first Joyful Mystery. Ave Maria's reflection highlights Mary's humility.

questions.prompt: Your child points to a sore knee after a tumble. As you comfort them, which sign can name the discomfort?
questions.explanation: Hurt uses two index fingertips moving toward each other with small motions near the relevant area. Continue responding to the child’s cues while you model it.

questions.prompt: Which mysteries does Ave Maria suggest for Thursday?
questions.explanation: The app pairs Thursday with the Luminous Mysteries. You can also choose another set for your prayer.

questions.prompt: A thumb-up fist rests on an open, upward-facing palm. Both hands lift together without separating. Which sign is it?
questions.explanation: Help keeps the fist and supporting palm connected as they rise. Lifting only the fist leaves out the coordinated two-hand movement.

questions.prompt: You hope to arrange your baby’s Baptism. What comes first?
questions.clue: Relatives are asking about dates, but you have not spoken with the parish.
options: Choose a date with relatives, then ask the parish to reserve it.
Ask the parish about preparation, timing, and required documents.
Ask another family what they needed and begin with that checklist.
questions.explanation: Start with your own parish’s requirements before fixing the family arrangements. Preparation and scheduling can vary.

questions.prompt: Watch the clip. Which family sign do you recognize?
questions.clue: Notice where the thumb meets the face.
questions.explanation: This is Mom: the thumb of an open hand touches or comes close to the chin. Dad uses a similar handshape at the forehead.

questions.prompt: Your baby needs feeding and comfort during Mass. What is the practical plan?
options: Meet the need, use a settling space if helpful, and rejoin worship when you can.
Let the parent holding him decide in the moment while the other stays seated.
Treat the care break as the end of this week’s family visit to church.
questions.explanation: Plan for real care needs as part of going to Mass. Your baby’s quietness is not a measure of faith.

questions.prompt: Which prayer contains this request for Mary's intercession?
questions.explanation: This line belongs to the Hail Mary. The request continues with prayer for us now and at the hour of our death.
questions.clue: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners,

questions.prompt: How can your baby join the family’s prayer before meals?
options: Begin participating once able to say the whole prayer with the family.
Be present while adults pray, with a simple invitation to join as skills grow.
Start with a separate prayer lesson before joining grace at the table.
questions.explanation: Adults can model a brief prayer now. Later, invite an “Amen” or something to thank God for.

questions.prompt: Complete this line from the Hail Mary.
questions.explanation: The Hail Mary names Jesus as the blessed fruit of Mary's womb.
questions.clue: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb,

questions.prompt: Your child hands you a toy. Which sign could you model to express gratitude?
questions.explanation: Thank you moves a straight, fingers-together hand forward from the chin toward the person. Pair it with a warm response when your child shares something.

questions.prompt: In the Visitation, whom does Mary visit?
questions.explanation: The second Joyful Mystery recalls Mary's visit to Elizabeth and her loving service.

questions.prompt: The index, middle, and ring fingers are extended; the thumb holds the little finger down. The index-finger side taps near the chin. Which sign fits?
questions.explanation: Water uses this three-finger handshape beside the chin. The location and handshape distinguish it from the cup-shaped hand used for Drink.

questions.prompt: Which family action connects naturally with Saint Joseph caring for Jesus and Mary?
options: Helping with a useful task for someone in the family.
Learning the names of every person in the Holy Family.
Choosing a favorite picture for the family prayer corner.
questions.explanation: A saint story can lead into one small act of service. The connection here is caring for the people entrusted to you.

questions.prompt: Which family sign matches this demonstration?
questions.clue: The location on the face is the key.
questions.explanation: This is Dad: an open hand brings its thumb to the forehead. The forehead location distinguishes it from Mom at the chin.

questions.prompt: How can you make Sunday departure less rushed?
questions.clue: Last week each parent thought the other had packed the changing supplies.
options: Divide supplies between two bags and have each parent choose what to bring.
Leave extra time to gather whichever supplies you notice on Sunday morning.
Check the bag the night before and name who carries it and handles changes.
questions.explanation: A checked bag and agreed roles remove a preventable decision at the door. Include changing supplies, feeding supplies, and an age-appropriate quiet book.

questions.prompt: In the app's standard Rosary opening, the three Hail Marys are offered for which virtues?
questions.explanation: The opening identifies the three Hail Marys with faith, hope, and charity before the mysteries begin.

questions.prompt: How does a parent pursue resilience during the newborn months?
questions.clue: Your newborn cries while you are talking about teaching him to handle challenges.
options: Respond to the need and save behavior expectations for later development.
Introduce a short, regular waiting exercise before ordinary comfort.
Keep the response identical each time so he learns one dependable routine.
questions.explanation: Newborn crying communicates needs rather than defiance. Steady care comes first; manageable play and later responsibilities provide other ways to practice skills.

questions.prompt: Name the short prayer that includes these words.
questions.explanation: The Glory Be praises the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. This line follows that opening praise.
questions.clue: as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be,

questions.prompt: You are about to roll a round, bouncy toy across the floor. Which sign names the object you are sharing?
questions.explanation: Ball uses two curved hands facing each other to outline a round shape. The fingertips approach, separate slightly, and meet again.

questions.prompt: Which words complete this opening of the Glory Be?
questions.explanation: The prayer names the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
questions.clue: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the

questions.prompt: One index finger stays upright while the other hand makes small peeling motions downward around its tip. Which food is being signed?
questions.explanation: Banana uses an upright supporting index finger and a peeling movement from the other hand. Keep the supporting finger still as the other hand moves.

questions.prompt: Your family chooses patience as this week’s virtue. Where should practice begin?
options: With a longer explanation of patience whenever the child gets frustrated.
With a daily question asking the child to name an example of patience.
With one visible act of patience by the adults each day.
questions.explanation: Give your child an example they can see in ordinary family life. Adults practice the character they hope to teach.

questions.prompt: What does the sign in this clip mean?
questions.clue: Watch the direction the palms turn.
questions.explanation: This is All done: both open hands turn from palms facing in to palms facing forward. It can mark the end of a meal, bath, or game.

questions.prompt: What is a simple way to keep a child’s Baptism part of family life?
options: Plan another large gathering every year to match the original celebration.
Mark its anniversary with prayer and tell the story as the child grows.
Save the story until the child is preparing for a later sacrament.
questions.explanation: Save the date, parish, godparents, and a photo. A brief anniversary prayer keeps the milestone familiar without needing a large event.

questions.prompt: Where does Ave Maria's Nativity reflection place the Infant Jesus?
questions.explanation: The Nativity is the third Joyful Mystery, reflecting on Jesus' birth at Bethlehem.

questions.prompt: You notice that your partner’s instruction creates a safety problem. What takes priority?
options: Calmly stop and correct it now, then talk through the disagreement afterward.
Keep the instruction consistent for now and revise the family rule privately.
Ask your child to pause while both parents debate the instruction together.
questions.explanation: Parental agreement must allow safety corrections. Ordinary disagreements can be discussed privately without leaving an unsafe instruction in place.

questions.prompt: In Ave Maria's Act of Contrition, what does the person resolve to do with God's grace?
options: Choose a mystery and count the beads
Name the day's gifts before a meal
Confess sins, do penance, and amend their life
questions.explanation: The prayer joins sorrow for sin with a resolve to change one's actions.

questions.prompt: On a walk, your child notices a barking animal on a leash. Which sign names it?
questions.explanation: Dog can be signed by patting the thigh with an open hand, as taught in Tiny Signs. Other ASL variants use a finger snap.

questions.prompt: Which prayer includes this appeal for mercy?
questions.explanation: The Fatima Prayer asks Jesus for forgiveness and mercy. Ave Maria includes it after the decades in its standard Rosary sequence.
questions.clue: lead all souls to Heaven, especially those in most need of Thy mercy.

questions.prompt: A bent index-finger knuckle lightly touches the cheek while the wrist twists a little. Which fruit is this?
questions.explanation: Apple uses the projecting knuckle of a bent index finger at the cheek. A small wrist twist completes the sign.

questions.prompt: Your toddler wants to stack a block but keeps missing. What help fits the goal?
options: Finish the tower together this time and choose a harder task tomorrow.
Give a small hint or steady the base, then let him make the next attempt.
Repeat the instructions from the beginning each time the block falls.
questions.explanation: Choose a challenge he can manage with a little support. Letting him attempt the useful part keeps him involved in the work.

questions.prompt: Which routine does this sign name?
questions.clue: Notice the hand lowering as the fingertips gather.
questions.explanation: This is Sleep: an open hand lowers from the upper face while the fingertips gather toward the thumb. The final shape is a flattened O rather than a tight fist.

questions.prompt: Which activity makes waiting practice manageable for a toddler?
options: Watching an adult finish a whole game before taking a first turn.
Short turns rolling a ball together, with help when needed.
Keeping the same turn length every day to measure improvement.
questions.explanation: Brief, supported turns give practice without turning the game into a test. Stop before frustration takes over.

questions.prompt: In the Guardian Angel Prayer, which word follows this line?
questions.explanation: The prayer asks the guardian angel to remain at our side, to light and guard, rule and guide.
questions.clue: ever this day be at my

questions.prompt: A grandparent will care for your toddler tomorrow. How should you prepare for consistent limits?
options: Describe every behavior you hope to improve so nothing is left uncertain.
Ask the grandparent to observe your routine first and infer the main rules.
Explain a few clear rules, the words you use, and the safe alternatives.
questions.explanation: A small set of clear expectations is easier to share and follow. Include what the child can do instead of only what to stop.

questions.prompt: Who presents Jesus in the Temple in the fourth Joyful Mystery?
questions.explanation: The Presentation recalls Mary and Joseph bringing Jesus to the Temple in obedience to God's law.

questions.prompt: The tub and towel are ready for the evening washing routine. Which sign can introduce the activity?
questions.explanation: Bath moves two loose fists a short distance up and down in front of the upper chest. Model it during setup, then continue the routine.

questions.prompt: Which Marian prayer contains this line?
questions.explanation: This line comes from Hail, Holy Queen, a closing prayer in Ave Maria's Rosary.
questions.clue: To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve.

questions.prompt: A flat hand with fingers together makes a small circle over the center of the chest. Which sign is it?
questions.explanation: Please uses a flat hand circling on the chest. Model it naturally when asking for something, without requiring a child to perform it.

questions.prompt: Your toddler raises a hand to hit during a game. What should your response include?
options: A question about why hitting feels tempting before changing the game.
Several choices about what the game’s rule should be from now on.
A short limit, preventing the hit, and showing a safe action instead.
questions.explanation: Keep the boundary clear and follow through calmly: “I won’t let you hit.” Stay close and show what to do instead.

questions.prompt: Which sign do these two hands make?
questions.clue: Look closely at the points of contact.
questions.explanation: This is More: the fingertips gather to each thumb, then the two fingertip groups meet. The gathered fingertips make contact rather than the whole palms clapping.

questions.prompt: Your toddler brings you your shoes. Which response models gratitude most clearly?
options: “Thank you for bringing my shoes. That helped me.”
“Good job! You’re always such a good helper.”
“Now tell me which polite word we use when someone helps.”
questions.explanation: A specific thank-you connects gratitude to the actual contribution. Model the words before expecting your child to use them.

questions.prompt: Which word completes this request to Saint Michael?
questions.explanation: The prayer calls on Saint Michael for protection against evil.
questions.clue: Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in

questions.prompt: You agree to own the diaper bag. What does that include?
options: Packing the supplies once your partner gives you the current list.
Checking, packing, carrying, and restocking it without waiting for reminders.
Carrying it on outings while your partner keeps track of what is missing.
questions.explanation: Owning a task includes noticing and preparing, as well as doing it. Make the full responsibility explicit between you.

questions.prompt: In the Finding in the Temple reflection, how long do Mary and Joseph seek Jesus?
questions.explanation: The fifth Joyful Mystery recalls their three-day search and the joy of finding Jesus in his Father's house.

questions.prompt: Before going outside, you show your child the clothing item that sits on top of their head. Which sign names it?
questions.explanation: Hat uses a flat, palm-down hand to pat the top of the head lightly. Show the real item as you model the sign.

questions.prompt: Which prayer asks for love to be kindled in the faithful?
questions.explanation: Come, Holy Spirit asks the Spirit to fill the faithful and renew the earth. Find it in Common prayers.
questions.clue: fill the hearts of Thy faithful and kindle in them the fire of Thy love.

questions.prompt: Two fists sit side by side with thumbs pointing upward. Their sides tap together twice near the lower chest. What does this name?
questions.explanation: Shoes uses two side-by-side fists tapping at their sides. Keep the thumbs up and the movement small.

questions.prompt: Your child takes a toy another child was using. What is a useful repair step?
options: Ask for a clear apology first, then work out what happens to the toy.
Help return the toy and model the words for making things right.
Move both children to a fresh activity and discuss the toy later.
questions.explanation: Responsibility includes a concrete action that repairs the problem. Help with the words without making the apology a performance.

questions.prompt: Which everyday action is shown here?
questions.clue: Follow the gathered fingertips.
questions.explanation: This is Eat: the fingertips gather to the thumb and move to the mouth. The compact handshape helps distinguish it from the C hand used for Drink.

questions.prompt: Small questions come up between routine appointments. What keeps them from getting lost?
options: Write them in one shared list as they occur and bring it to the visit.
Keep separate mental lists and compare them in the waiting room.
Choose the single most memorable question on the morning of the visit.
questions.explanation: Capture useful questions when they arise so both parents can contribute. Urgent concerns need prompt care rather than waiting on a routine list.

questions.prompt: Which garden is named in the first Sorrowful Mystery?
options: The garden near the empty tomb
questions.explanation: The Agony in the Garden recalls Jesus praying in Gethsemane and accepting the Father's will.

questions.prompt: What makes a handoff useful to the next parent?
questions.clue: You are changing shifts after a busy evening.
options: The recent feed, diaper, and sleep, plus what helped and what comes next.
A complete account of the evening in the order each event happened.
A description of how the evening felt, leaving practical details for questions.
questions.explanation: Give the next parent the information needed to continue care. A short, current snapshot is easier to use than a long narrative.

questions.prompt: Which prayer expresses sorrow using these words?
questions.explanation: The Act of Contrition expresses sorrow for sin and a resolve to amend one's life.
questions.clue: I am heartily sorry for having offended Thee

questions.prompt: At the aquarium, a small animal with fins swims past the glass. Which sign connects to what your child sees?
questions.explanation: Fish uses one flat hand moving forward while wiggling from side to side. The sideways-facing palm and flowing movement suggest swimming.

questions.prompt: Which virtue does Ave Maria pair with the Carrying of the Cross?
questions.explanation: The app's reflection names patience while contemplating Jesus carrying the Cross to Calvary.

questions.prompt: Beside the mouth, the thumb and index finger open and close like a small beak while the other fingers stay folded. Which animal is it?
questions.explanation: Bird opens and closes the thumb and index finger beside the mouth. The other fingers remain folded.

questions.prompt: You spoke sharply to your partner in front of your child. How can you model accountability?
options: Discuss it privately and rely on a calmer tone for the rest of the day.
Explain the stressful circumstances so your child understands the reaction.
Acknowledge the mistake, apologize, and show a better response.
questions.explanation: Children can see adults take responsibility and begin again. A clear apology plus changed action makes repair visible.

questions.prompt: Which action matches the clip?
questions.clue: Notice the curved hand and its short arc.
questions.explanation: This is Drink: a C hand moves toward the mouth as if tipping a cup. Keep the curved handshape throughout the small movement.

questions.prompt: The baby’s and your partner’s hospital bags are packed. What practical step is easy to overlook?
options: Adding more newborn outfits to cover every possible length of stay.
Waiting to pack your things until the hospital confirms what is available.
Packing your own clothes, toiletries, snacks, and chargers.
questions.explanation: Prepare your own essentials too. That lets you stay present without needing a last-minute supply trip.

questions.prompt: Which family prayer begins with these words?
questions.explanation: Grace Before Meals asks God to bless us and the gifts we are about to receive.
questions.clue: Bless us, O Lord, and these Thy gifts,

questions.prompt: Which night-shift agreement is the clearest?
options: Agree that the more rested parent will decide who takes each waking.
Name who is on duty, the stretch covered, and the care each parent owns.
Split the number of tasks equally and choose their timing during the night.
questions.explanation: Agree on responsibilities before everyone is tired. Fit the arrangement around the baby’s feeding plan and both parents’ rest.

questions.prompt: Which mystery comes first in the Glorious Mysteries?
questions.explanation: The Glorious Mysteries begin with Jesus rising from the dead, followed by the Ascension.

questions.prompt: Your child stops to notice colorful petals on a stem in the garden. Which sign names what caught their attention?
questions.explanation: Flower gathers the fingertips toward the thumb beside the nose, then moves the hand from one side of the nose to the other. Connect the sign to the plant you are noticing together.

questions.prompt: Which prayer contains this rhyming request?
questions.explanation: The Guardian Angel Prayer asks the angel to stay at our side and guide us.
questions.clue: to light and guard, to rule and guide.

questions.prompt: One elbow rests on the other hand. The forearm stays upright while the spread hand twists like moving branches. Which sign fits?
questions.explanation: Tree uses an upright forearm supported at the elbow, with the open hand twisting above it. The arm and spread fingers suggest a trunk and branches.

questions.prompt: Your toddler is shy when greeting a visitor. How can you keep teaching manners?
options: Greet the visitor yourself and invite a wave, sign, or word he can manage.
Wait quietly until he says hello before you begin the adult conversation.
Save greeting practice for when he can use all four polite words reliably.
questions.explanation: Model the greeting and match the invitation to his communication skills. Manners take practice and do not require adult-level performance.

questions.prompt: Which object does this sign represent?
questions.clue: Watch how the palms open while the little-finger edges stay together.
questions.explanation: This is Book: flat hands start palm to palm and open upward while their little-finger edges stay together. The motion resembles opening its covers.

questions.prompt: Your toddler can do one step of getting dressed, but it takes longer. How can you practice responsibility?
options: Allow extra time and let him do that step, helping with the rest.
Do the whole task on weekdays and wait for him to manage it independently.
Ask him to complete the full routine each time so the responsibility is clear.
questions.explanation: Give him a real part he can manage. Keep helping where needed while making room for practice.

questions.prompt: Which mystery contemplates Mary being taken body and soul into heaven?
questions.explanation: The Assumption concerns Mary being taken into heaven. The Ascension concerns Jesus ascending into heaven.

questions.prompt: Relatives want to visit during the first week at home. What is the best preparation?
options: Accept tentative plans now and settle the length of each visit on arrival.
Have each parent handle their own relatives using their own preferences.
Agree together on who visits, when, and for how long before answering.
questions.explanation: A shared plan lets both parents give the same answer. It also reduces decisions and negotiation during the first days at home.

questions.prompt: Which prayer begins with this appeal to Mary?
questions.explanation: The Memorare asks for Mary's intercession with confidence in her help. The app includes its full traditional text.
questions.clue: Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary, that never was it known

questions.prompt: Through the window, you watch drops fall from the clouds and splash into puddles. Which weather sign fits?
questions.explanation: Rain lowers both hands in short, repeated movements with the fingers spread and slightly bent. Both palms face down.

questions.prompt: At which event does Mary tell the servants to do whatever Jesus tells them?
questions.explanation: The second Luminous Mystery is the Wedding at Cana. Its reflection focuses on trust in Mary's intercession.

questions.prompt: A loose claw-shaped hand starts near the mouth, then moves away and turns outward. Which temperature sign is this?
questions.explanation: Hot begins with a curved hand near the mouth and moves outward with a turn. The starting palm faces toward you.

questions.prompt: Your partner is settled feeding the baby and has no drink or meal within reach. What help fits best?
options: Wait until the feed ends so you can decide together which job matters most.
Bring food and water, then handle the nearby household job you already own.
Offer several possible tasks and ask your partner to assign them to you.
questions.explanation: Notice the practical need and complete a useful task. Support includes preparation and follow-through, not only availability when asked.

questions.prompt: Which animal is signed in this clip?
questions.clue: Notice the small outward movement beside the cheek.
questions.explanation: This is Cat: the thumb and index finger pinch and move outward beside the mouth. The movement suggests tracing a whisker.

questions.prompt: Your toddler declines a suitable food he has not tried before. What is a useful next step?
options: Ask for one taste each time so the meal always includes a new experience.
Keep the invitation optional and offer the food again another day.
Remove it from the family rotation until he requests it himself.
questions.explanation: Offer variety without required bites. A refusal today does not need to become either a contest or a permanent decision.

questions.prompt: Which three apostles are named in Ave Maria's Transfiguration reflection?
questions.explanation: The fourth Luminous Mystery recalls Jesus being transfigured in glory before Peter, James, and John.

questions.prompt: Your baby is content exploring a toy on a safe floor space beside you. What should you do?
options: Introduce another toy whenever he repeats the same action several times.
Turn the play into a short lesson with a sequence for him to complete.
Stay attentive, let him lead for a while, and respond when he seeks you.
questions.explanation: Make room for his own exploring alongside shared play. Stay available; a chance to try does not require isolation.

questions.prompt: Which event is the fifth Luminous Mystery?
options: The Descent of the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: The final Luminous Mystery reflects on Jesus giving himself to us in the Eucharist.

questions.prompt: Outside, the air is chilly and you pull your jacket closer while shivering. Which sign describes that feeling?
questions.explanation: Cold uses two loose fists facing each other in front of the chest. A slight shaking movement resembles shivering.
